books.section: Regional Differences in British North America
The Evolution of Governance in Colonial North America

options.text: Massachusetts limited voting to church members; Pennsylvania's Frame gave an assembly and toleration.

options.misconception: Massachusetts had a General Court; Pennsylvania had no king.
options.text: Massachusetts had no assembly at all, while Pennsylvania was ruled by a king.

options.misconception: Pennsylvania promised toleration; it did not ban religion.
options.text: Pennsylvania banned all religion entirely, while Massachusetts required church attendance.

options.misconception: Neither colony was ruled directly by Parliament; both had assemblies.
options.text: Both colonies were ruled directly by Parliament in London, with no assemblies.

rationales.A: Passage A says only church members could vote or hold office in Massachusetts, and the colony enforced a single faith by banishing Williams in 1636 and Hutchinson in 1638. Passage B says Penn's Frame of Government of 1682 gave settlers an elected assembly and promised religious toleration to different faiths. Background: Massachusetts had a General Court, so it did have an assembly; Pennsylvania had no king and was not ruled directly by Parliament. The difference is who could take part and whether one faith ruled.
rationales.B: Massachusetts had a General Court; Pennsylvania had no king.
rationales.C: Pennsylvania promised toleration; it did not ban religion.
rationales.D: Neither colony was ruled directly by Parliament; both had assemblies.
rationales.general:
1. Read Passage A. In Massachusetts only church members voted, and one faith was enforced.
2. Read Passage B. In Pennsylvania the Frame gave an elected assembly and promised toleration.
3. Compare the two. One colony narrowed who could take part; the other widened it.
4. Drop the rest. Massachusetts had an assembly, Pennsylvania had no king, and neither was ruled directly by Parliament.
Remember: compare the rules of the game — who votes and who worships tells you the government.

source: original; stimulus is an original secondary passage written for this question
stem: According to the passages, how did Massachusetts and Pennsylvania differ?

stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passages written for this question; facts from the grounding books.
stimulus.text:
Passage A — Massachusetts: "In Massachusetts, government and church were one. Only church members could vote or hold office, and the colony's leaders enforced a single faith — Roger Williams was banished in 1636 and Anne Hutchinson in 1638 for preaching ideas the leaders rejected. The General Court made the laws, but it answered to the colony's Puritan ministers as much as to its voters."

Passage B — Pennsylvania: "In Pennsylvania, William Penn's Frame of Government (1682) gave settlers an elected assembly and promised religious toleration. Penn welcomed Quakers, Lutherans, Catholics, and Jews, and the colony's government was designed to let different faiths live side by side. Penn called it a 'holy experiment' in government by consent."
